text: {"claims": [{"id": "c0", "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S0", "rel": "entails"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P4.S0 states verbatim that before 4.0 writable replicas could not expire keys with a TTL; version comparison already verified."}, {"id": "c1", "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S0", "rel": "entails"}, {"sid": "P4.S1", "rel": "entails"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P4.S0 sets the pre-4.0 writable-replica context and P4.S1 says using EXPIRE makes the key leak, still counted and using memory."}, {"id": "c3", "evidence": [{"sid": "P4.S2", "rel": "entails"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P4.S2 states 4.0 RC3 and greater evict TTL keys as masters do, except keys written in DB numbers greater than 63."}, {"id": "c4", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "P4.S2 only says by default instances have 16 databases; the stronger 'never applies' is not stated, since DB count is configurable."}, {"id": "c5", "evidence": [{"sid": "P1.S4", "rel": "entails"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P1.S4 states that since Redis 4.0 all sub-replicas receive exactly the same replication stream from the master; version check holds."}, {"id": "c6", "evidence": [], "check": null, "reasoning": "P5.S0 only describes behaviour since 4.0 (writes local, not propagated); the passages say nothing about propagation on Redis 3.0."}, {"id": "c8", "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S0", "rel": "refutes"}, {"sid": "P9.S0", "rel": "refutes"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P7.S0 says asynchronous replication means you cannot ensure a replica received a write, so loss is always possible; P9.S0 calls it best effort, not guaranteed."}, {"id": "c9", "evidence": [{"sid": "P8.S2", "rel": "entails"}, {"sid": "P9.S0", "rel": "entails"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "P8.S2 allows configuring a max replica lag in seconds; P9.S0 says the data-loss window is restricted to that given number of seconds."}]}
